title: Indian Tenancy Laws — Model Tenancy Act 2021 and State Variations

central_act.name: Model Tenancy Act 2021
central_act.type: Model legislation (states may adopt with modifications)
central_act.objective: To establish a fast-track adjudicating mechanism, balance rights of landlords and tenants, and bring rental housing into the formal economy.

key_provisions.detail: Every tenancy must be created through a written tenancy agreement between landlord and tenant. The agreement must be submitted to the Rent Authority within 2 months of execution.
Security deposit shall not exceed two months' rent for residential premises.
Security deposit shall not exceed six months' rent for non-residential premises.
Landlord must refund security deposit within one month of vacation/handover of possession, after deducting any dues.
Rent can only be revised as per the terms of the tenancy agreement. In absence of such provision, rent can be revised with three months' prior notice.
Structural repairs and major maintenance are the landlord's responsibility. Day-to-day minor repairs (fixtures, appliances) are the tenant's responsibility unless agreed otherwise.
Tenant cannot sub-let without written consent of the landlord.
Landlord cannot withhold essential services (water, electricity, sanitation) even if there is a rent dispute.

Eviction disputes are adjudicated by the Rent Authority (District Collector-level officer). Appeals lie to the Rent Court (Civil Court of District Judge level), and further to the Rent Tribunal (High Court level).
On expiry of the tenancy agreement, if the tenant refuses to vacate, the landlord can approach the Rent Authority for eviction order within 3 months.

notice_periods.landlord_to_tenant: Minimum 15 days for non-payment of rent; 30 days for other grounds

eviction_grounds: Non-payment of rent for two consecutive months
Premises required for landlord's own use or bona fide use by family member
Tenancy obtained by fraud or misrepresentation
tenant_rights: Right to obtain receipt for rent paid
Right to peaceful enjoyment of premises
Right to have structural repairs done by landlord
Right to refund of security deposit within one month of vacation
Right to challenge arbitrary eviction before Rent Authority
Right to receive at least 24 hours' notice before landlord entry
Right to sub-let with written consent of landlord
landlord_rights: Right to receive rent on agreed date
Right to inspect premises with prior notice
Right to evict on legal grounds through proper process
Right to withhold security deposit against dues
Right to revise rent with agreed notice period
Right to recover possession on expiry of tenancy

Maharashtra.applicability: Applies to premises in areas declared by state government; excludes premises with monthly rent above ₹15,000 (in some areas) — check latest notification
Maharashtra.administering_authority: Court of Small Causes (Mumbai); Civil Court (other areas)

key_provisions.detail: Tenants protected even after expiry of fixed-term agreement; cannot be evicted without court order on specific grounds.
Concept of 'standard rent' — fair rent fixed by court. Landlord cannot charge more than standard rent.
Recognises the historic 'pagdi' (premium/pugree) system under which tenants pay a lump-sum premium and lower monthly rent. Tenant has right to sell pagdi rights with landlord's consent.
Tenancy rights pass to family members residing with tenant on death of tenant.

security_deposit.residential: Typically 2 months' rent (no statutory cap under old Act; Model Tenancy Act 2021 cap applies in notified areas)

eviction_grounds: Landlord's bona fide need (own use or family)
Material alteration or damage to premises
Using residential premises for commercial purpose
Permanent vacation of premises by tenant
Maharashtra.rent_increase_limit: Permitted increase as per agreement or court-fixed standard rent; increases not generally allowed more than once in 3 years without court order in protected tenancies
courts: Civil Court (District level) for other cities

Karnataka.applicability: Applies to residential and non-residential premises in areas notified by the state government; does not apply to premises constructed after 2001 in some categories.
Karnataka.administering_authority: Rent Controller (Civil Judge); District Court (Appeal); High Court (Second Appeal)

key_provisions.detail: Tenancy agreement should be in writing and registered if more than 11 months.
No statutory cap under Karnataka Rent Act 1999; in practice 10 months' deposit common in Bengaluru. Karnataka has adopted Model Tenancy Act 2021 principles.
Landlord must issue rent receipt within 3 days of receiving rent.

security_deposit.residential: Up to 10 months' rent (common practice in Bengaluru); Model Tenancy Act 2021 adopts 2 months cap

Karnataka.rent_increase_limit: 5% per annum after first 5 years of tenancy; requires notice

Delhi.act_name: Delhi Rent Control Act 1958 (for older tenancies); Model Tenancy Act 2021 (adopted 2023)
Delhi.applicability: Delhi Rent Control Act 1958 applies to premises with monthly rent up to ₹3,500 (as notified). Premises above this threshold governed by Transfer of Property Act and Delhi's adoption of Model Tenancy Act.
Delhi.administering_authority: Rent Controller (Additional District Judge); Rent Control Tribunal (District Judge); High Court

key_provisions.detail: For premises under ₹3,500/month, tenant has statutory protection; eviction only on specific grounds.
Governed by Transfer of Property Act 1882 and Model Tenancy Act 2021 (as adopted). Standard contract terms apply.
Most Delhi residential arrangements structured as 'Leave and Licence' to avoid Rent Control Act protections. 11-month agreements common to avoid registration.

security_deposit.residential: 2 months' rent (Model Tenancy Act cap); in practice 2-3 months
security_deposit.commercial: Up to 6 months (Model Tenancy Act cap)

eviction_grounds: Tenant having another suitable accommodation in Delhi
Delhi.rent_increase_limit: 10% per annum increase permissible with proper notice under the old act; as per agreement under new framework

Tamil Nadu.act_name: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017
Tamil Nadu.applicability: Applies to all residential and non-residential premises in Tamil Nadu except those exempted.
Tamil Nadu.administering_authority: Rent Authority (Revenue Divisional Officer); Rent Court (Subordinate Court); Rent Tribunal (District Court)

key_provisions.detail: Tenancy agreement must be submitted to Rent Authority within 90 days of execution. Failure makes tenancy unenforceable.
Residential: maximum 2 months' advance rent. Non-residential: maximum 3 months' advance rent.
Subletting prohibited without written consent of landlord.

Telangana.act_name: Telangana Rent Control Act 1960 (for older premises); Model Tenancy Act 2021 adopted
Telangana.applicability: Applies in Hyderabad and notified areas for premises below certain rent thresholds.
Telangana.administering_authority: Rent Controller; City Civil Court; Telangana High Court

key_provisions.detail: Advance rent (deposit) limited to 10 months rent for residential premises under the old Act; 2 months under Model Tenancy Act.
Concept of 'fair rent' — tenant can apply to Rent Controller to fix fair rent if charging exceeds fair rent.

security_deposit.residential: 2-10 months (common practice); legally 2 months under Model Tenancy Act

Telangana.rent_increase_limit: No increase within first year; thereafter as per agreement or court order

leave_and_licence.description: A Leave and Licence agreement grants the licensee the right to use the premises for a specified period. Unlike a lease, it does not create an interest in property and can be revoked. 11-month agreements are typically Leave and Licence to avoid compulsory registration and rent control protection.
leave_and_licence.key_difference_from_lease: Lease creates an interest in immovable property (Transfer of Property Act); Leave and Licence does not. Lease tenants get stronger eviction protection under Rent Control Acts.

registration.mandatory: Leases exceeding 11 months must be registered under the Registration Act 1908.
registration.stamp_duty: Lease/Leave and Licence agreements attract stamp duty (state-specific; typically 0.25-2% of total rent for the period).
registration.unregistered_lease: An unregistered lease for more than one year is inadmissible as evidence under Section 49 Registration Act 1908.

relevant_sections: Section 106 — Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract (month-to-month / year-to-year)
Section 108 — Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee
Section 114 — Relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent
